ble_219_0c046ee8.name: NMI_Handler
ble_219_0c046ee8.description: Cortex-M NMI vector target. It is an empty infinite loop, so any NMI hangs the core until the watchdog (if enabled) resets the chip.

ble_219_0c046eec.name: startup_copy_vector_table_to_sram
ble_219_0c046eec.summary: Copy the flash vector table into SRAM at 0x20000000
ble_219_0c046eec.description: Word-copy loop that reads consecutive 32-bit words from the vector table inside the RAW4TFT image (header + 0x400, starting at the initial-SP word) and stores them at 0x20000000, 0x20000004, ... It stops after the word that is vector_IRQ75_Handler has been copied, i.e. it relocates the exception table plus 75 IRQ entries to SRAM so handlers can be patched at run time. Called from ble_219_0c046f24 (early startup code).
ble_219_0c046eec.notes: Source start address is derived from raw4tft_header.padding+0x3cc, which decodes to the vector table at 0x0C028400.

params.name: param_1
params.description: slot index into the word array at 0x2000f4cc

returns.description: true if the slot is non-zero

ble_219_0c047644.name: crc16_ccitt_nibble
ble_219_0c047644.summary: Table-driven CRC-16/CCITT (poly 0x1021, MSB first) over a buffer, 4 bits at a time
ble_219_0c047644.description: Computes a CRC-16 with polynomial 0x1021 using a 16-entry nibble table at 0x0C08097C (entries 0x0000, 0x1021, 0x2042, ...). For each byte the high nibble is processed first, then the low nibble: crc = table[nibble ^ (crc >> 12)] ^ ((crc & 0xFFF) << 4). param_1 optionally points to a context of u16 values: [0] is the initial CRC and [2] (offset 4) is a final XOR value; if NULL both are 0. param_4 is a stride: the data pointer advances by param_4 bytes per step and the remaining length is decremented by param_4 per step (normally 1). Returns xorout ^ crc. Called from five places, including the NB upgrade/UART frame code paths (ble_219_0c0285ec, 0c02d784, 0c02dc50, 0c0366e4, 0c037798).

params.name: param_1
params.description: optional CRC context: u16 init at +0, u16 xor-out at +4; NULL means 0/0

params.name: param_4
params.description: step/stride in bytes (1 for contiguous data)

ble_219_0c0476a0.name: crc32_reflected_table
ble_219_0c0476a0.summary: Table-driven reflected CRC-32 (poly 0xEDB88320) over a buffer
ble_219_0c0476a0.description: Standard byte-wise CRC-32: crc = table[(byte ^ crc) & 0xFF] ^ (crc >> 8) with the 256-entry table at 0x0C074168. param_1 optionally points to a context of two u32 words: [0] initial CRC value, [1] final XOR value (NULL means both 0), so the caller supplies 0xFFFFFFFF/0xFFFFFFFF for the usual IEEE CRC-32. param_4 is a stride: pointer advances by param_4 and the remaining count drops by param_4 per iteration. Returns xorout ^ crc. Used for firmware/IAP image CRC verification and other integrity checks (callers ble_219_0c034468, 0c03457c, 0c047274).

params.name: param_1
params.description: optional context: u32 init at +0, u32 xor-out at +4; NULL = 0/0

ble_219_0c0476d8.name: md5_encode_le_words
ble_219_0c0476d8.description: Do-while loop that takes consecutive 32-bit words from param_2 and writes each as four bytes (LSB first) to param_1 until at least param_3 bytes have been produced; because it is a do-while, at least one word is always written and the length is effectively rounded up to a multiple of 4. This is the MD5 'Encode' helper used to write out the state words as the 16-byte digest; its only caller is ble_219_0c047efc (MD5 final).

params.name: param_3
params.description: number of bytes to produce (multiple of 4)

ble_219_0c047710.name: md5_transform
ble_219_0c047710.summary: MD5 compression function: process one 64-byte block into the 4-word state
ble_219_0c047710.description: Fully unrolled 64-step MD5 (RFC 1321, constants such as 0xD76AA478, 0xE8C7B756 ...; rotates 7/12/17/22, 5/9/14/20, 4/11/16/23, 6/10/15/21). param_1 points to the four state words A,B,C,D (a context pointer plus 8 in the surrounding MD5 context); param_2 is the 64-byte input block which is first decoded into sixteen little-endian words on the stack. After the rounds the result is added back into the state in place. Called from the MD5 update routine ble_219_0c047e70. Used by the firmware-upgrade module for the md5sum check.

params.name: param_1
params.description: state A,B,C,D (4 x u32), updated in place

ble_219_0c047e44.name: md5_init
ble_219_0c047e44.description: Zeroes the 64-bit bit-count words at ctx[0],ctx[1] and loads the standard MD5 initial values into ctx[2..5]: 0x67452301, 0xEFCDAB89, 0x98BADCFE, 0x10325476. Called from ble_219_0c03477c, ble_219_0c036868 and ble_219_0c0369d8 (md5sum computation in the upgrade code).

params.name: param_1
params.description: MD5 context (6 x u32: count lo/hi, state A..D)

ble_219_0c047fe8.description: Single return instruction with no side effects. Called from ble_219_0c043f48 as an empty hook.

ble_219_0c048b00.name: ble_ring_dispatch_pending
ble_219_0c048b00.summary: Drain a ring of queued callbacks until the read index meets the write index
ble_219_0c048b00.description: Reads write index DAT_2000f7b0 and read index DAT_2000f7c0 (u16). While they differ it fetches entry #read from a table at DAT_2000f7b8 (8 bytes per entry: function pointer at +0, u16 value at +4) and calls fn(DAT_2000f7b4 + read * DAT_2000f7bc, entry.u16, ...), i.e. the first argument is the address of the read-th element of a parallel buffer (base DAT_2000f7b4, element size DAT_2000f7bc). Afterwards the read index is incremented and wrapped to 0 once it passes the last index DAT_2000f7be. Called from ble_219_0c0599d4 (looks like a deferred completion/event dispatch for a DMA or transport ring).
ble_219_0c048b00.notes: Exact subsystem (UART/HCI transport DMA completion vs. other event queue) not determined.

ble_219_0c048f34.name: bthost_tlv_get_instance
ble_219_0c048f34.summary: Return the pointer to the flash TLV storage vtable
ble_219_0c048f34.description: Returns the address 0x0C07FFFC of a constant three-entry function table (btstack_tlv_t: get_tag, store_tag, delete_tag, code at 0x0C048DEC/0x0C048CAC/0x0C048B70). Called from ble_219_0c05b67c, which also calls the link-key DB get_instance, so it is the BTstack TLV (tag-length-value persistent store) implementation handed to the bthost key/device databases.

returns.description: pointer to the TLV implementation vtable

ble_219_0c048f34.notes: Identification as btstack_tlv_t is inferred from how the link-key and device DB call vtable slots +0 (get) and +8 (delete).

ble_219_0c048f3c.name: aes128_key_expansion
ble_219_0c048f3c.summary: AES-128 key schedule: expand a 16-byte key into 176 bytes of round keys
ble_219_0c048f3c.description: Copies the 16-byte key from param_2 to param_1, then generates words 4..43: each new word is the previous word XOR the word four positions back; every fourth word first applies RotWord, SubWord via the AES S-box at 0x0C083E20, and XORs the round constant from the table at 0x0C07482C (0x01,0x02,0x04,...,0x1B,0x36). Output is the 11 round keys (44 words = 176 bytes) at param_1. Called together with ble_219_0c048fd4 from the three AES wrappers ble_219_0c049288, 0c0493d4, 0c0496a8.

ble_219_0c048fd4.name: aes128_encrypt_block
ble_219_0c048fd4.summary: AES-128 ECB encrypt of one 16-byte block, in place, using an expanded key
ble_219_0c048fd4.description: Standard byte-oriented AES-128 encryption: initial AddRoundKey, nine rounds of SubBytes (S-box at 0x0C083E20), ShiftRows, MixColumns (GF(2^8) xtime with reduction constant 0x1B) and AddRoundKey, then a final round without MixColumns. param_1 is the 176-byte schedule from ble_219_0c048f3c and param_2 the 16-byte state which is overwritten with the ciphertext. Used by the BLE crypto wrappers (ble_219_0c049288, 0c0493d4, 0c0496a8), e.g. for AES-ECB/CCM-style operations and authentication.

ble_219_0c0499f0.name: sha1_ctx_init_with_seed
ble_219_0c0499f0.summary: Initialise a SHA-1 style context, optionally loading four state words
ble_219_0c0499f0.description: Zeroes the 64-bit length counter ctx[0],ctx[1] and ctx[6] (the fifth state word E, which in ble_219_0c049a28 is stored at offset 0x18). If param_2 is non-NULL, four words are copied from it into ctx[2..5] (the A,B,C,D state words); if NULL those words are left untouched. Unlike plain SHA-1 init this does not write the fixed constants, so the caller supplies the initial vector. Caller: ble_219_0c02bdd0.

params.name: param_1
params.description: hash context (7 x u32: length lo/hi, A,B,C,D,E)

params.name: param_2
params.description: optional 4-word initial state (A,B,C,D); NULL to keep existing

ble_219_0c0499f0.notes: Role of the 4-word seed is unverified; may be a keyed/seeded hash construct.

ble_219_0c049a20.name: sha1_ctx_set_e_word_one
ble_219_0c049a20.summary: Set the word at offset 0x18 of a context to 1
ble_219_0c049a20.description: Stores 1 in *(u32*)(param_1+0x18). In the SHA-1 context used by ble_219_0c049a28 offset 0x18 is the fifth state word, but this function has no direct callers, so it is more likely a generic 'set flag' method reached through a function-pointer table.

ble_219_0c049a28.name: sha1_process_block
ble_219_0c049a28.summary: SHA-1 compression: process one 64-byte block into the five-word state
ble_219_0c049a28.description: Fully unrolled 80-round SHA-1 (constants 0x5A827999, 0x6ED9EBA1, 0x8F1BBCDC, 0xCA62C1D6; rotl 5 / rotl 30). The state A,B,C,D,E lives at ctx+8,+0xC,+0x10,+0x14,+0x18. The 16 input words at param_2 are byte-swapped (big-endian load) into W[0..15] and the schedule W[t] = rotl1(W[t-3]^W[t-8]^W[t-14]^W[t-16]) is computed on the fly. Results are added back into the state in place and 0 is returned. Called from ble_219_0c04a924 (SHA-1 update/final wrapper).

ble_219_0c04ab90.name: bthost_link_key_db_tlv_iterator_get_next
ble_219_0c04ab90.summary: Link-key DB iterator: fetch the next stored link key from TLV storage
ble_219_0c04ab90.description: Iterator state is a byte index in *param_1 (0..3, max four entries). For each index it calls the TLV get_tag function (*DAT_2000f8ac) with context DAT_2000f8b0, tag 0x42544C00|index ('BTL'+index) and a 28-byte buffer. On the first tag that exists it copies the 6-byte BD_ADDR to param_2, the 16-byte link key to param_3 and the u16 key type to param_4, advances the index and returns 1. If none is found, the index becomes 4 and 0 is returned. This is slot 7 of the BTstack btstack_link_key_db_t vtable at 0x0C07FE88 (hence no direct callers); source file bthost_link_key_db_tlv.c.

returns.description: 1 if an entry was returned, 0 when iteration is finished

ble_219_0c04ade0.name: bthost_link_key_db_tlv_get_instance
ble_219_0c04ade0.summary: Register the TLV implementation/context and return the link-key DB vtable
ble_219_0c04ade0.description: Stores the TLV implementation pointer in DAT_2000f8ac and its context in DAT_2000f8b0 (used by the link-key DB functions to read/write tags 'BTL'+index), then returns the address 0x0C07FE88 of the btstack_link_key_db_t function table (open, set_local_bd_addr, close, get/put/delete_link_key, iterator_init/get_next/done). Called from ble_219_0c05b67c during host initialisation.

returns.description: pointer to link key DB vtable

Its only caller, ble_219_0c04bd98, uses it with the companion ble_219_0c04c578, which extracts the upper five bits of the same byte, so the byte is a packed field with a 3-bit part and a 5-bit part (e.g. a type/length style header).

ble_219_0c04cbb4.name: att_validate_security
ble_219_0c04cbb4.summary: Check whether a connection's security level satisfies an ATT attribute's permissions
ble_219_0c04cbb4.description: BTstack att_db.c security check. param_3 is the attribute iterator whose flags (u16 at +6) hold the read/write permission bits and, in the top nibble, the required encryption key size (stored as size-1). param_2 selects the operation (1 = write, otherwise read) which decides which flag bits form the required level 0..3 (1 encrypted, 2 authenticated, 3 authorized). param_1 is the att_connection_t: encryption_key_size at +7, authenticated at +8, authorized at +9, and a flag at +10 that switches to a variant of the check. Returns the ATT error code: 0x05 insufficient authentication, 0x08 insufficient authorization, 0x0F insufficient encryption, 0x0C insufficient encryption key size, or 0 when allowed. Called from ble_219_0c04ceb8 (attribute read/write handler).

params.name: param_1
params.description: ATT connection state (key size, authenticated, authorized)

params.name: param_3
params.description: ATT attribute iterator; flags u16 at +6

ble_219_0c04cbb4.notes: Bit-level mapping inferred from decompilation against att_db.c; the +10 connection flag is believed to be secure-connection state.

Called from ble_219_0c04e702 when a connection ends or the prepared-write queue is reset.

params.name: param_1
